steps.title: Nineteen styles, five ideas
steps.body: The list is long but the families are short: tube, tape, transformer, clipping, and the deliberately broken ones. Knowing which family you want narrows it to three.

steps.title: Tube — soft, asymmetric, forgiving
steps.body: Adds mostly even harmonics and rounds peaks gradually. Clean Tube barely colours; Broken Tube is an effect. This is the family to reach for when you are not sure.

steps.title: Tape — compression you hear as thickness
steps.body: Softens transients before it adds harmonics, so drums come back sounding glued rather than distorted. Push Drive further here than you would on a tube style.

steps.title: Transformer — weight at the bottom
steps.body: Low-frequency saturation with a gentle high-end loss. Useful on bass and on a whole mix at low drive, where it reads as size rather than as distortion.

steps.title: Rectify and Foldback — not colour, effects
steps.body: Rectify folds the negative half of the waveform; Foldback turns peaks back on themselves. Both generate harmonics unrelated to the source, which is the point. Use small amounts of Mix.

steps.title: Every style is gain-matched
steps.body: At any drive, the output level stays within a tenth of a decibel of the input. You can turn Drive up and hear only what it does to the character, which is the only honest way to choose a style.
